dial.summary: BTC Accumulation holds on Sep 11 as 5 of 8 indicators remain supportive — Global M2 still expanding, 2s10s steepened to +43bps, Fed balance sheet stable at $6.74T, BTC funding near zero (~0.01%), and stablecoin dominance in a sustained 30-day downtrend (11.2% on $2.74T TOTAL); real yields have shifted to headwind (derived ~2.56% as 10Y nominal reached 4.96% — cusp of 5% — following hot Aug PPI +5.4% YoY and CPI Aug 2026 release today); DXY ticked up to 99.06 but remains in the neutral 97.5–100 band; BTC.D at 57.2% holds above the 55% alt-rotation threshold despite BTC pulling back to ~$76,900 (-1.6%); Sep 16 FOMC hike probability ~57% — the week's ECB (Sep 10 hike confirmed), FOMC (Sep 16), BOE (Sep 17), and BOJ (Sep 18) cluster is the defining risk event for Q4 2026 trajectory.

indicators.name: Global Liquidity (Global M2)
indicators.note: Global 4-bank M2 aggregate (Fed/ECB/BOJ/PBOC) estimated at ~$103.4T (July 2026 composite; 6–8 week reporting lag means August aggregate unavailable until mid-October); MacroMicro confirmed June 2026 global G4 M2 at $102,663.81B ($102.66T); July YoY growth rates at 4.67–4.81% per MacroMicro; broader global broad money supply (all central banks) reached a record $150T in June 2026 per SpendNode Sep 2 report — G4 aggregate of $103.4T consistent with this (G4 ≈ 69% of global total); 4-week uptrend confirmed on July G4 composite vs June confirmed ($102.66T → ~$103.4T = +$0.74T, above flat threshold); August global 4-bank aggregate not yet published (expected mid-October); status supportive (4-week rising trend met); ECB hiked Sep 10, FOMC Sep 16 (~57% hike probability), and BOJ Sep 18 — the full September central bank sequence will determine Q4 global liquidity trajectory.

indicators.name: ISM Manufacturing PMI
indicators.note: August 2026 ISM Manufacturing PMI released Sep 1 at 54.6%, down 1.0pp from July 55.6% (eighth consecutive month of expansion; below 55.2% consensus); Production 58.3% (−0.2pp), New Orders 53.7% (−3.0pp vs July), Backlogs 51.8% (−3.2pp), Employment 51.2% (−1.6pp); 4-week trend down: July 55.6% → August 54.6% = −1.0pp; ISM Non-Manufacturing PMI (Sep 3) was 55.4% (beat 54.1% forecast); status neutral (above 50 but falling; supportive requires above 50 AND rising; headwind requires below 48 and falling or above 62 — neither applies); reading of 54.6% corresponds to approximately 2.4% annualized real GDP growth per ISM historical correlation; next ISM Manufacturing release October 1 (September data); S&P Global Flash PMI Sep 23 will provide the next advance manufacturing-sector read.

indicators.name: DXY (US Dollar Index)
indicators.note: ICE DXY at 99.06 on September 11, 2026 — up +0.32% from Sep 10 (98.75) as the global bond selloff (10Y at 4.96%, cusp of 5%) lends marginal USD support; 4-week trend down: from approximately 101.0–101.4 in early August to 99.06 on Sep 11 = −2.0% relative decline, well above the 0.5% flat threshold; status neutral (ICE DXY 99.06 within 97.5–100 band; approaching but not yet at the 100 headwind threshold); dollar has weakened ~0.96% over the past month per Trade Weighted index data; Aug PPI came in hot (+0.4% MoM, +5.4% YoY per BLS Sep 10 release) — headline energy-driven by diesel (+24.1%); Aug CPI released today (Sep 11, 8:30 AM ET, consensus 3.4% YoY); if CPI reinforces the inflation narrative, DXY could break above 100 into headwind territory ahead of FOMC Sep 16 (~57% hike odds); FOMC dot plot and rate path guidance are the primary remaining DXY catalyst.

indicators.name: Real Yields (US10Y - CPI)
indicators.note: Derived real yield: 10Y nominal 4.96% (Sep 11 Bloomberg — cusp of 5%, +16bps on the day) minus 10Y BEI estimated 2.40% (T10YIE range 2.2%–2.5% per FRED; mid-range applied given stable core CPI near-2.4%) = ~2.56%; FRED direct DFII10 fetch blocked again this run; last confirmed DFII10 value: 2.42% as of Sep 3–4, 2026 (ALFRED database cutoff); 4-week trend up: ~2.43% (Aug 11 estimate) → ~2.56% (Sep 11 derived) = +13bps, above the 5bps flat threshold — trend flipped from flat to up; status headwind (rising 4-week trend AND value above 2%); this headwind status is new vs Sep 10 (was neutral/flat); key driver is the global bond selloff pushing 10Y toward 5% following hot Aug PPI (+5.4% YoY, Sep 10) and ahead of Aug CPI (Sep 11); FOMC Sep 16 and dot plot are the primary catalyst — a hike + hawkish 2027 dots would likely push real yields further above 2.5%, deepening the headwind for risk assets.

indicators.name: 2s10s Yield Curve
indicators.note: September 11, 2026: 2s10s spread at approximately +0.43% (+43bps); Sep 11 data: 10Y yield 4.96% (Bloomberg — cusp of 5%), 2Y yield 4.535% (up +14.5bps from Sep 10's 4.39%), spread = 4.96% − 4.535% = +42.5bps, reported as +0.43%; 4-week uptrend confirmed: ~+35bps (Aug 9 estimate) → +43bps (Sep 11) = +8bps net steepening over 4 weeks; status supportive (positive spread AND 4-week steepening confirmed; well outside the −50bps headwind threshold); note: today's steepening is a 'bear steepener' — both yields rising, 10Y faster than 2Y — driven by inflation/fiscal concerns rather than rate-cut expectations; FOMC Sep 16 is the key near-term risk: a hike would rapidly flatten the curve as 2Y reprices faster; the curve remains solidly in positive territory compared to the deeply inverted (−50bps+) range of 2023–24.

indicators.name: Fed Balance Sheet
indicators.note: WALCL: $6.74T (~$6,737B) for week ending September 2, 2026 (H.4.1 confirmed; govspending.org cross-reference); H.4.1 for week ending September 10 was released at 4:30 PM ET September 10 — not yet captured in this run (FRED API blocked; no govspending.org Sep 10 data confirmed in search results); 4-week trend flat: ~Aug 5 estimate ~$6.70T → Sep 2 $6.74T = +$40B, within flat threshold; status supportive (holding at post-2022 stabilization plateau; routine measured QT continues with no acceleration and no overnight rate spike); the Sep 10 H.4.1 report would reflect the post-ECB rate decision (Sep 10 hike) and pre-FOMC (Sep 16) reserve conditions; next confirmed update expected when FRED API access is restored.

indicators.name: BTC Funding Rates (perps avg)
indicators.note: BTC perpetual funding rate at approximately +0.01% per 8h (Sep 9–11, 2026; CoinGlass direct fetch egress-blocked; value cross-referenced from MacroMicro BTC perpetual futures funding rate series showing 0.01% for Sep 9–10 context); 30-day trend flat: near zero throughout August–September 2026; BTC.D at 57.2% (Sep 11: $1.54T BTC market cap / $2.74T TOTAL — BTC down 1.6% to $76,900 on CPI release day volatility); well below the +0.04% per 8h overheating threshold; status supportive (near-zero funding confirms spot-driven price action with no leveraged long crowding; slight pullback in BTC today is orderly and unaccompanied by funding rate spike); BTC.D decline from 57.48% (Sep 10) to 57.2% (Sep 11) reflects broader crypto market selling slightly outpacing BTC — not yet at the 55% alt-rotation threshold.

indicators.name: Stablecoin Dominance
indicators.note: Stablecoin market cap ~$307B (Sep 11, 2026; stablecoinbeat.com and CoinGecko cross-reference); total crypto market cap $2.74T (Sep 11: down 1.9% / −$0.053T from Sep 10's $2.78T, driven by BTC −1.6% to $76,900 on CPI day volatility); stablecoin dominance 11.2% on Sep 11 ($307B / $2.74T) — ticked up from 11.04% (Sep 10) as crypto market fell while stablecoin supply held flat; 30-day trend down: from ~13–14% in early August 2026 to 11.2% = sustained ~2–3pp decline confirming capital deployment into risk assets over the past month; status supportive (30-day falling trend confirmed; headwind condition — dominance rising while TOTAL also rising — does NOT apply: today's dominance uptick is caused by falling TOTAL, not fresh TOTAL growth; structural 30-day trend remains down); USD stablecoins (USDT + USDC) hold ~83% of the $307B stablecoin supply.

upcoming.title: Empire State Manufacturing Survey (September 2026)
upcoming.note: Federal Reserve Bank of New York Empire State Manufacturing Business Conditions Index for September 2026 at 8:30 AM ET — one of the earliest September manufacturing reads; August 2026 survey showed prices paid surging to 58.6 (from 52.3 in July) and inventories at -5.2, suggesting cost-push pressures building in the Northeast manufacturing sector; a strong September reading would reinforce the ISM-above-50 expansion backdrop heading into FOMC Sep 16; a sharp decline would introduce doubts about the manufacturing recovery sustainability; leading indicator for ISM Manufacturing (next release October 1).

upcoming.title: FOMC Rate Decision (September 2026)
upcoming.note: Federal Reserve FOMC rate decision at 2:00 PM ET (two-day meeting Sep 15–16), press conference at 2:30 PM ET; includes updated Summary of Economic Projections (SEP) with dot plot; current target range 3.5%–3.75% (held at July 28–29 meeting); market-implied hike probability ~57% (CME FedWatch Sep 11) following Aug NFP beat (+162K vs +56K consensus, Sep 4) and hot Aug PPI (+5.4% YoY, Sep 10); CPI Aug (Sep 11) is the final data input before the decision; dot plot and 2027 rate path guidance are the primary DXY, real yield, and risk-asset drivers for Q4 2026; a hike + hawkish dots would push real yields higher and test the 5% nominal 10Y level; a dovish hold preserving a cut pathway would be the most risk-on outcome for crypto.

upcoming.title: Retail Sales (August 2026)
upcoming.note: Census Bureau Advance Monthly Retail Sales for August 2026 at 8:30 AM ET — released same day as FOMC decision (2:00 PM ET); prior July advance retail sales were +0.1% MoM; strong Aug NFP (+162K) suggests continued consumer income growth supporting spending; a strong retail sales print (+0.3% MoM or above) confirms Q3 consumer resilience and may reinforce the Fed's inflation-fighting case; a weak print (below 0%) would suggest consumer fatigue despite labor market strength, potentially complicating the Fed's policy calculus.

upcoming.title: Industrial Production (August 2026)
upcoming.note: Federal Reserve Board Industrial Production and Capacity Utilization for August 2026 at 9:15 AM ET — released same day as FOMC; measures output of manufacturing, mining, and electric and gas utilities; a strong reading would reinforce ISM Manufacturing's expansion signal (54.6 in August) and reduce near-term recession concerns; capacity utilization approaching 80% would add to inflationary pressures and potentially reinforce the FOMC hike case; context: Aug PPI energy component surged (diesel +24.1% MoM) due to Middle East conflict spillovers — watch energy sector output.

upcoming.title: Bank of England Rate Decision (September 2026)
upcoming.note: Bank of England Monetary Policy Committee rate decision at 12:00 PM London time (7:00 AM ET) — one day after FOMC Sep 16; BOE currently holds at 3.75% (July 30 MPC vote 6-3 to hold, with Pill, Greene, and Mann voting to hike to 4.00%); UK CPI at 2.9% YoY in July, elevated by Middle East energy spillover; if ECB hiked Sep 10 and FOMC hiked Sep 16, a BOE hold with dovish guidance would create significant transatlantic monetary policy divergence driving GBP/EUR and GBP/USD volatility; a surprise BOE hike would confirm the global tightening cycle remains synchronized; BOE outcome will significantly influence risk sentiment heading into the last two weeks of September.

upcoming.title: Housing Starts & Building Permits (August 2026)
upcoming.note: Census Bureau Housing Starts and Building Permits for August 2026 at 8:30 AM ET — a leading indicator for residential construction activity and broader economic momentum; released same day as BOE decision; higher rates (FOMC possibly hiking Sep 16) weigh on housing affordability; a decline in starts or permits would add to evidence that elevated financing costs are cooling the housing sector despite a resilient labor market; context for mortgage rates: 30Y fixed mortgage rates have been elevated in the 6.5–7.5% range in 2026 due to the rate environment.

upcoming.title: Philadelphia Fed Manufacturing Survey (September 2026)
upcoming.note: Federal Reserve Bank of Philadelphia Manufacturing Business Outlook Survey for September 2026 at 8:30 AM ET — released same day as BOE rate decision; a leading indicator for national ISM Manufacturing (next release Oct 1); prior August reading showed moderate expansion; released alongside Initial Jobless Claims; a strong Philly Fed print would reinforce the ISM-above-50 backdrop and reduce near-term recession risk; the index is one of the earliest September manufacturing reads and helps calibrate expectations for ISM Manufacturing on October 1.

upcoming.title: Initial Jobless Claims (week ended September 13, 2026)
upcoming.note: DOL weekly initial jobless claims at 8:30 AM ET for week ending September 13, 2026 — first labor market read post-FOMC Sep 16; any significant spike above 220K would amplify rate-path repricing following the FOMC decision; prior week ending Sep 6 came in at approximately 206K; released same day as BOE rate decision and Philadelphia Fed Manufacturing Survey.

upcoming.title: Bank of Japan Rate Decision (September 2026)
upcoming.note: Bank of Japan Monetary Policy Meeting September 17–18, with Statement on Monetary Policy expected September 18 — two days after FOMC Sep 16; BOJ has been normalizing policy in 2026 (hiked June 16); any surprise hike or hawkish commentary would strengthen JPY and potentially trigger yen-carry-trade unwinds with broad impact on global risk assets including crypto; DXY at 99.06 on Sep 11 (partial recovery from 98.75 low) — a hawkish BOJ would accelerate dollar weakness toward the supportive sub-97.5 threshold; the full ECB (Sep 10 hike) + FOMC (Sep 16) + BOJ (Sep 18) sequence within one week is the most synchronized global monetary policy event cluster of the cycle and will set the tone for Q4 2026.
